creatures-a.why: B turns the Long One from an unreadable blown-out clump into a clear fanged serpent and sharpens the Mimic's bite. It loses some Kindled glow, which should be taken from A.

creatures-b.why: B fixes the two weakest creatures: the Polyps become readable spined animals and the Riptide gains its eye and loses the space-like starfield; the Brinewyrm's threat end also reads better. Frostbloom is identical in both.

quarters-room.why: Same room, but B replaces A's wet-mirror floor streaks with satin pools, varies the wall bays, and lights the furnishings (star chart, bunk sconce, galley, shelf), so light lands warmly and bought things look cared for.

furnishings.why: A's items are better lit and read better: star chart, books and bunk sconce. Its palettes have real structural differences, not just a tint. B only wins on the kettle material and the rug profile.

wings.why: B's crisper stones and glinting creatures make both wings read more as showpieces; A is warmer and cozier in the hall but its bloom swallows the specimens. The margin is small.
